metric.code_efficiency_conciseness.method: Manual inspection of template/programs/java/micro (mb00-mb11) and adversarial samples. Java requires explicit type declarations, boilerplate class wrapper, explicit access modifiers, manual loop indices, and verbose System.out.printf/Locale ceremony for numeric formatting compared to more concise languages. Java 16+ records (used in mb04, mb09 for multi-value Result types) reduce boilerplate versus classic POJOs, and var type-inference plus enhanced for-loops help conciseness in idiomatic modern Java, but mandatory class enclosure and lack of top-level functions keep token counts higher than more concise peers for equivalent algorithmic content.
observations: mb04.java (~72 lines) implements a 4-accumulator floating point workload; a terser language typically needs fewer structural lines due to no mandatory class wrapper and less explicit typing.

mb09.java repeats explicit double[] declarations and manual loops for mean/variance/correlation/histogram computation; idiomatic Java stays close to raw loop form since vectorized library shortcuts would violate fairness rules, but explicit typing and required class/method scaffolding add overhead relative to inferred-type languages.
Adversarial programs (ADV series) show standard Java ceremony (explicit class declaration, main(String[] args) signature, exception handling boilerplate) required on every entry point.
metric.code_efficiency_conciseness.scale_note: 0-100, 100 = maximally concise/efficient-to-write for equivalent, idiomatic, non-degraded implementation. Java scored 66: solid modern idioms (records, var, enhanced-for, streams) available, but mandatory OOP scaffolding and verbose declarations impose real per-line overhead versus terser peers.

metric.readability.method: Manual inspection of the same micro (mb00-mb11) and adversarial program corpus for naming clarity, structural organization, comment density, and cognitive load of idiomatic Java constructs.
observations: Consistent naming conventions (Lcg, Result, workload()) and doc-style comments in mb04/mb09 make algorithmic intent clear; explicit static typing on every field/variable aids readability by making data flow and units unambiguous.
record types (Result(double s1, double s2, double s3, double s4)) communicate immutable multi-value returns compactly and readably, superior to raw tuples or untyped maps.
Explicit block braces, consistent 4-space indentation, and one-statement-per-line style keep nested loops (mb09 moment/correlation/histogram passes) easy to follow despite algorithmic density.

Minor readability costs: verbose exception/generic boilerplate and required System.out.printf(Locale.ROOT, ...) ceremony for locale-safe numeric formatting, more explicit than higher-level languages but not harmful to comprehension.
metric.readability.scale_note: 0-100, 100 = maximally readable for an experienced engineer with no external context. Java scored 83: strong static typing and naming conventions aid comprehension; verbosity slightly increases visual scanning cost but does not obscure algorithmic intent.
